kandoInfo.heading: Kando Martial Arts Knox
description: Kando Martial Arts was established in 1997 by Chief Instructor Shihan Paul Veldman, a highly respected martial arts instructor with decades of experience.
Shihan Paul is a 6th Degree Black Belt in Karate and began training at age 13, later specialising in traditional Shukokai Karate.
Sensei Andy started karate at a young age and developed confidence, resilience, and leadership through years of dedicated training.
With over a decade of teaching experience, Sensei Andy now leads Kando Martial Arts Knox, delivering high-quality karate instruction to families from across the Knox area.
Kando Martial Arts Knox proudly supports students travelling from Rowville with structured, traditional karate training.

getToKando.heading: Getting to Kando Martial Arts Knox from Rowville
description: Rowville families exploring karate and martial arts options often choose Kando Martial Arts Knox for our comprehensive programs that cater to different age groups and skill levels. Our Boronia location serves Rowville residents who are looking for more than just physical activity—they want their children to learn discipline, respect, and self-confidence through authentic karate training.

The journey from Rowville to our Boronia dojo typically takes around 15 to 20 minutes by car. Take Stud Road heading north toward Boronia, then turn onto Burwood Highway. From Burwood Highway, turn into Lewis Road, followed by a turn into Wadhurst Drive. Our facility is located at Unit 2/5 Wadhurst Drive, Boronia.

While Rowville is a bit further from Boronia, many families make the trip because they appreciate our teaching philosophy and the positive impact our programs have on children's development. Rowville students often become dedicated members, regularly attending classes and progressing through the belt system while building lasting friendships. The commitment shown by Rowville families reflects their dedication to their children's martial arts education and personal growth, and we're honoured to be part of their journey.
